one-sample-t-test.def: A significance test of $H_0: \mu = \mu_0$ for a population mean when $\sigma$ is unknown, using the t distribution with $n - 1$ degrees of freedom. A paired t test is a one-sample t test on the differences of paired data, usually with $H_0: \mu_d = 0$.

mu-null.def: The hypothesized mean $\mu_0$: the value of the population mean stated by the null hypothesis $H_0: \mu = \mu_0$. It comes from the question (a claim, a standard, a past value), never from the sample.
